body: U.S. Bank National Association, as trustee for the registered holders of the Morgan Stanley Bank of America Merrill Lynch Trust 2016-C28, filed suit on August 12, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey against Lenox Drive Office Park LLC, a Delaware company that owns office buildings on Lenox Drive in Mercer County, Mortgage Professional America reported. Greystone Servicing Company handles the loan. Lenox Drive Office Park LLC bought Princeton Pike Corporate Center in Lawrenceville in early 2016, NJB Magazine reported at the time.

According to the complaint as reported, Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. made a $130 million loan to the borrower in December 2015, split across several promissory notes and secured by a mortgage on the office park along with cash-management agreements and UCC filings on rents and fixtures. The loan matured on January 1, 2026, and the trust says it was not repaid. As of July 1, 2026, the trust says $141,767,219.75 was owed, including principal, interest at the note and default rates, late fees and servicing charges, with interest still accruing.

The trust seeks an order foreclosing and selling the property and the appointment of a receiver to run the office park during the case and conduct the sale. The federal docket shows a clerk's entry of default on October 8, 2026, an amended complaint on October 29, and an entry titled "Appoint Receiver" on November 6. No court has ruled on the merits.

timeline.label: Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. makes the $130M loan, later held by the 2016-C28 trust
Loan matures and, the trust says, is not repaid
U.S. Bank, as trustee, sues to foreclose and seeks a receiver
Clerk enters default after the plaintiff's request (docket entry 6)
Plaintiff files an amended complaint (docket entry 10)
Docket records an "Appoint Receiver" entry (docket entry 11)
